*   Goal: Find the time (When) and distance from the station (Where) when Train 2 catches up to Train 1.

    *   Train 1 starts at 14:05.
    *   Train 2 starts at 14:35.
    *   Time difference ($\Delta t$) = 14:35 - 14:05 = 30 minutes.
    *   Convert minutes to hours: 30 minutes = 0.5 hours.

    *   In that 30-minute head start, how far has Train 1 traveled?
    *   Distance = Speed $\times$ Time
    *   $d_{headstart} = 80 \text{ km/h} \times 0.5 \text{ h} = 40 \text{ km}$.

    *   Train 2 is faster than Train 1.
    *   Relative speed ($v_{rel}$) = $v_2 - v_1 = 110 \text{ km/h} - 80 \text{ km/h} = 30 \text{ km/h}$.
    *   This means Train 2 closes the gap at a rate of 30 km every hour.

    *   Time to close the gap ($t_{catchup}$) = $\frac{\text{Gap distance}}{\text{Relative speed}}$
    *   $t_{catchup} = \frac{40 \text{ km}}{30 \text{ km/h}} = \frac{4}{3} \text{ hours}$.
